name: Lou Reed
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember packing children's books before clothes on moving day.” People around Lighthouse Cove know Lou by a small Saturday habit. Lou takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I moved without giving him the new number because I needed one quiet Christmas. I can say that to his face now.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for a moss-green cardigan and a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. Lou has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, with a high puff tied with plain cord. Lou listens with the head tilted a little to the left during a conversation.
personality: Lou enjoys routines and will defend the right of someone else to break one. As a result, Lou is often everyone's favorite cover for a missed morning.
agenda: To tell the father why the new address was withheld.
family: Opal Felix is Lou’s cousin raised in the same household. Their relatives kept a holiday fund in a boot that still had its mate. Even after the family acquired bank accounts, an envelope of change at supper meant somebody was planning a journey. Lou asks whether the person being visited is ready for company. Asked about *The other side of the cove*, Opal says, “I saved the original donor letter. It specified a sea view and made no mention of who's looking.”
connections: Douglas Waters. Two households sort out where letters ought to go without making a public forwarding list.

reactions.situation: A child wants to leave the homecoming meal early
reactions.response: Lou gives the child an ordinary excuse to step outside without suggesting they reject the father.

reactions.response: Lou takes it to a staffed counter with a second person present and leaves contact details for the owner.
